## Objective
- Improve the existing game so its advertised sound works and taking the elevator leads to a longer, goal-driven experience with suspense.

## Requirements
- Build a complete, playable game or apply the requested changes to the existing game; do not ask clarifying questions.
- Make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (maximum 1280px wide) and inspect only the latest one.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- (none)

### Active
- Fix or implement game audio.
- Add a clear goal, more gameplay, and suspense around using the elevator.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the existing game and identify its audio and elevator/gameplay flow.
2. Implement working sound and a more substantial, goal-oriented suspenseful elevator experience.
3. Test playability and inspect a current screenshot; report assumptions and changes briefly.

## Relevant Files
- (none)

## Important Context
- The user’s feedback: “Das Spiel ist gut aber es hat kein Ton, obwohl es steht mit Ton und es geht so schnell vorbei ohne Ziel. Ohne Spannung, wenn man Elevator nimmt.”

- Improve the existing game so its advertised sound works and the elevator leads to a longer, goal-driven experience with suspense.

- Apply changes to the existing game without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

- Improve the goal-driven gameplay and suspense around calling and taking the elevator.

- (none)

1. Implement and verify working audio.

- User feedback: “Das Spiel ist gut aber es hat kein Ton, obwohl es steht mit Ton und es geht so schnell vorbei ohne Ziel. Ohne Spannung, wenn man Elevator nimmt.”
- The current game already has three keycards, a generator objective, a 180-second detonation timer, and a 60-second elevator-survival phase; the elevator interaction currently calls the lift and later boards it at the same panel.
- No files have been changed yet.

## Objective
- Improve the existing game so its advertised sound works and the elevator leads to a longer, goal-driven experience with suspense.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected audio, objectives, elevator, and interaction flow; no files have been changed.

### Active
- Fix or implement reliable game audio.
- Improve goal-driven gameplay and suspense around calling and taking the elevator.
- Test playability and inspect a current screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect relevant game logic and audio implementation in `src/game.js`.
2. Implement reliable audio and a more suspenseful elevator progression.
3. Test playability and inspect the latest screenshot, saved as a JPEG no wider than 1280px.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Game logic, audio, objectives, monster, and elevator interactions.
- `index.html`: Game UI, audio toggle, and objective display.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and overlays.
- `capture-run.mjs`: Browser screenshot capture workflow.

## Important Context
- User feedback: “Das Spiel ist gut aber es hat kein Ton, obwohl es steht mit Ton und es geht so schnell vorbei ohne Ziel. Ohne Spannung, wenn man Elevator nimmt.”
- Existing game has three keycards, a generator objective, a 180-second detonation timer, and a 60-second elevator-survival phase.
- Audio uses generated Web Audio tones; it activates only after user interaction, and mute state suppresses playback.
- Elevator interaction currently requires restoring the generator, surviving the hold, then interacting with the same panel to escape.

- Apply changes to the existing game without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

- Audio uses generated Web Audio tones; playback is suppressed when muted, and browsers may require user interaction before audio starts.
- The elevator requires restoring the generator, surviving the hold, then interacting with the same panel to escape.

set -euo pipefail

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

PROJECT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
cd "$PROJECT_DIR"
PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
BUILD_DIR="$PROJECT_DIR/.omgithub-runtime/dist"
DEPLOYMENT_FILE="/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-web/deployment-output.json"

run() {
  /usr/bin/time -p "$@"
}

run npm ci --no-audit --no-fund

HAS_BUILD="$(run node -e 'const p=require("./package.json"); process.stdout.write(p.scripts?.build ? "yes" : "no")')"
if [[ "$HAS_BUILD" == yes ]]; then
  run npm run build
  BUILD_DIR="$PROJECT_DIR/dist"
else
  run rm -rf "$BUILD_DIR"
  run mkdir -p "$BUILD_DIR"
  run cp -a index.html style.css src assets vendor "$BUILD_DIR/"
fi

[[ -f "$BUILD_DIR/index.html" ]] || { echo "Built static entry point not found: $BUILD_DIR/index.html" >&2; exit 1; }
run mkdir -p "$(dirname "$DEPLOYMENT_FILE")"
run env PROJECT_DIR="$PROJECT_DIR" BUILD_DIR="$BUILD_DIR" DEPLOYMENT_FILE="$DEPLOYMENT_FILE" node -e '
  const fs = require("node:fs");
  const path = require("node:path");
  const metadata = { project: process.env.PROJECT_DIR, directory: path.resolve(process.env.BUILD_DIR) };
  fs.writeFileSync(process.env.DEPLOYMENT_FILE, JSON.stringify(metadata) + "\n");
'

# Keep the static server in the foreground so the controller can monitor it.
run python3 -m http.server "$PORT" --bind 0.0.0.0 --directory "$BUILD_DIR"

- Sound is toggled by `#sound-toggle`; browser audio playback may require a user gesture.
- Changes are uncommitted; no tests or screenshot checks have been completed.

## Objective
- Improve sound reliability and extend the elevator sequence into a longer, goal-driven experience with more suspense.

## Requirements
- Apply changes without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use a shared Web Audio master gain and a low-level ambient sound bed to improve audio reliability and suspense.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `ensureAudio`, `setAudioScene`, `setMasterVolume`, and routed tones through `masterGain` in `src/game.js`.
- Added audio state declarations and initialized a filtered ambient bed with a master gain.

### Active
- Integrate audio scene and master-volume updates with menu, gameplay, ending, mute, and volume-slider handlers.
- Strengthen the elevator wait and escape sequence with clearer goals and suspense.
- Test the updated flow and capture/inspect only the latest JPEG within the specified size limit.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Wire `setAudioScene()` and `setMasterVolume()` into game states and UI handlers; the sound toggle currently does not update the master gain.
2. Refine the elevator sequence, which currently starts a 60-second survival phase and then permits escape from the same panel.
3. Run and test the game flow; capture and inspect the latest JPEG at no more than 1280px wide.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Audio, game states, objectives, monster behavior, elevator interactions, gameplay loop; modified and uncommitted.
- `index.html`: Sound toggle, volume control, objective display, and game UI.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and overlays.
- `capture-run.mjs`: Browser screenshot capture workflow.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.

## Important Context
- User feedback: “Das Spiel ist gut aber es hat kein Ton, obwohl es steht mit Ton und es geht so schnell vorbei ohne Ziel. Ohne Spannung, wenn man Elevator nimmt.”
- `setAudioScene()` and `setMasterVolume()` exist but are not yet integrated with game states and slider events.
- `game.liftDelay` was added to the run state but is currently unused.

## Objective
- Improve sound reliability and extend the elevator sequence into a longer, goal-driven experience with more suspense.

## Requirements
- Apply changes without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use a shared Web Audio master gain and a low-level ambient sound bed to improve audio reliability and suspense.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added audio helpers and initialized a filtered ambient bed with a master gain in `src/game.js`.
- Added `game.liftDelay` to run state, but it is unused.

### Active
- Integrate `setAudioScene()` and `setMasterVolume()` with menu, gameplay, ending, mute, and volume-slider handlers.
- Strengthen the elevator wait and escape sequence; it currently begins a 60-second survival phase and allows winning from the same panel afterward.
- Test the updated flow and capture/inspect the latest JPEG within the specified size limit.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Wire `setAudioScene()` and `setMasterVolume()` into game states and UI handlers; the sound toggle does not update master gain, and no volume-slider input handler was found.
2. Refine the elevator sequence and use or remove the currently unused `game.liftDelay`.
3. Run and test the game flow; capture and inspect only the latest JPEG at no more than 1280px wide.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Audio helpers, game states, objectives, monster behavior, elevator interactions, gameplay loop; modified and uncommitted.
- `index.html`: Sound toggle, volume control, objective display, and game UI.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and overlays.
- `capture-run.mjs`: Existing browser screenshot workflow currently saves PNGs at 1440px desktop and 390px mobile widths.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.

## Important Context
- User feedback: “Das Spiel ist gut aber es hat kein Ton, obwohl es steht mit Ton und es geht so schnell vorbei ohne Ziel. Ohne Spannung, wenn man Elevator nimmt.”
- `setAudioScene()` and `setMasterVolume()` exist but are not yet integrated with game states and slider events.
- The lift interaction at `src/game.js:112` starts the 60-second survival timer and permits winning by interacting with that same panel afterward.

## Objective
- Improve sound reliability and extend the elevator sequence into a longer, goal-driven experience with more suspense.

## Requirements
- Apply changes without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use a shared Web Audio master gain and a low-level ambient sound bed to improve audio reliability and suspense.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added audio helpers and initialized a filtered ambient sound bed with master gain in `src/game.js`.
- Added `game.liftDelay` to run state, but it is unused.

### Active
- Integrate `setAudioScene()` and `setMasterVolume()` with menu, gameplay, ending, mute, and volume-slider handlers.

- Test the updated flow and capture/inspect the latest JPEG within the specified size limit.

- (none)

1. Wire `setAudioScene()` and `setMasterVolume()` into game states and UI handlers; the sound toggle does not update master gain, and no volume-slider input handler was found.

- `src/game.js`: Audio helpers, game states, objectives, monster behavior, elevator interactions, gameplay loop; modified and uncommitted.

- `style.css`: Game presentation and overlays.
- `capture-run.mjs`: Existing browser screenshot workflow currently saves PNGs at 1440px desktop and 390px mobile widths.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.

- `setAudioScene()` and `setMasterVolume()` exist but are not yet integrated with game states and slider events.
- The lift interaction at `src/game.js:112` starts the 60-second survival timer and permits winning by interacting with that same panel afterward.

## Objective
- Improve sound reliability and extend the elevator sequence into a longer, goal-driven experience with more suspense.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use a shared Web Audio master gain and a low-level ambient sound bed.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added audio helpers and initialized filtered ambient audio with master gain in `src/game.js`.
- Added `game.liftDelay` to run state.

### Active
- Connect audio scenes and volume updates to game states and UI, including sound toggle and `#volume-slider`.
- Refine the elevator sequence and use or remove `game.liftDelay`.
- Test the updated flow; capture and inspect the latest JPEG within the size limit.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Wire audio updates to menu, gameplay, ending, mute, and volume-slider events.
2. Strengthen the elevator sequence; currently the 60-second survival timer starts on the first lift-panel interaction, and the same panel wins once it expires.
3. Run the game flow and test it.
4. Capture a JPEG no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Audio helpers, game states, objectives, monster behavior, elevator interactions, gameplay loop; modified and uncommitted.
- `index.html`: Sound toggle, volume control, objectives, and game UI.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and overlays.
- `capture-run.mjs`: Existing screenshot workflow captures PNGs at 1440px desktop and 390px mobile widths.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.

## Important Context
- User feedback: “Das Spiel ist gut aber es hat kein Ton, obwohl es steht mit Ton und es geht so schnell vorbei ohne Ziel. Ohne Spannung, wenn man Elevator nimmt.”
- `setAudioScene()` and `setMasterVolume()` exist but are not yet integrated with game states and slider events.
- `game.liftDelay` is currently unused.
- `git status` showed only `src/game.js` modified.

## Objective
- Improve sound reliability and extend the elevator sequence into a longer, goal-driven experience with more suspense.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use a shared Web Audio master gain and a low-level ambient sound bed.
- The elevator sequence uses a 60-second survival timer; after it expires, the player must return to the lift panel to win.
- Remove `game.liftDelay` if it remains unused.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added filtered ambient audio and shared master-gain helpers in `src/game.js`.
- Removed `game.liftDelay`; added elevator timer, cue, door, and indicator state.
- Reworked the surface elevator entrance with sliding doors, a panel indicator, survival countdown cues, and door-opening behavior after the timer expires.
- Connected gameplay start and ending states to ambient audio.

### Active
- Integrate the sound toggle and volume slider with the shared master gain.
- Refine and verify elevator interactions, suspense cues, and post-timer return-to-panel win condition.
- Test the updated game flow and capture/inspect the latest JPEG within the specified size limit.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Wire `#sound-toggle` and `#volume-slider` events to `setMasterVolume()` and ensure audio resumes on user interaction.
2. Verify the lift doors open and the player can enter and win by returning to the panel after the 60-second survival timer.
3. Run the game flow and check for errors.
4. Save and inspect only the latest JPEG, no wider than 1280px.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Audio helpers, game states, elevator construction/interactions, gameplay loop, and UI events; modified and uncommitted.
- `index.html`: Sound toggle and volume control.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and overlays.
- `capture-run.mjs`: Existing screenshot workflow; currently captures PNGs at 1440px desktop and 390px mobile widths.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.

## Important Context
- The existing sound-toggle handler changes `muted` but does not call `setMasterVolume()`; the volume slider has no registered handler.
- Elevator changes have not yet been tested; latest edits include countdown cues and a door animation after the timer.

## Objective
- Improve sound reliability and extend the elevator sequence into a longer, goal-driven experience with more suspense.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use a shared Web Audio master gain and a low-level ambient sound bed.
- The elevator sequence uses a 60-second survival timer; after it expires, the player must return to the lift panel to win.
- Remove `game.liftDelay` if it remains unused.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added filtered ambient audio and shared master-gain helpers in `src/game.js`.
- Added elevator timer, countdown cues, sliding doors, panel indicator, and return-to-panel win interaction.
- Connected gameplay start and ending states to ambient audio.
- Wired `#sound-toggle` and `#volume-slider` to the shared master gain; sound toggle now calls `setMasterVolume()`.
- `node --check src/game.js` and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Verify sound toggle and volume slider in the browser.
- Verify the 60-second elevator sequence, opening doors, and return-to-panel win condition.
- Check browser flow for errors and capture/inspect the latest JPEG within the size limit.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run the game in a browser and test sound controls.
2. Verify the elevator countdown, door opening, and return-to-panel win interaction.
3. Check for browser errors.
4. Save and inspect only the latest JPEG, no wider than 1280px.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Audio helpers, elevator interactions, gameplay loop, and sound UI event handlers; modified and uncommitted.
- `index.html`: Sound toggle and volume control.
- `capture-run.mjs`: Existing screenshot workflow captures PNGs at 1440px desktop and 390px mobile widths.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.

## Important Context
- The countdown starts when the powered elevator is called; the monster activates, suspense cues play, and the panel indicator turns green when the timer expires.
- The elevator doors animate open after the timer, and interacting with the panel again wins.
- The existing capture workflow does not meet the JPEG/1280px requirement without adjustment.

## Objective
- Improve sound reliability and extend the elevator sequence into a longer, goal-driven experience with more suspense.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use a shared Web Audio master gain and a low-level ambient sound bed.
- The elevator sequence uses a 60-second survival timer; after it expires, the player must return to the lift panel to win.
- Remove `game.liftDelay` if it remains unused.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added ambient audio, shared master-gain helpers, elevator countdown cues, sliding doors, panel indicator, and return-to-panel win interaction in `src/game.js`.
- Connected gameplay start and ending states to ambient audio; wired `#sound-toggle` and `#volume-slider` to the shared master gain.
- `node --check src/game.js` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Browser checks confirmed sound toggle, slider gain, gameplay ambience, elevator call and 60-second countdown, and doors opening/clearing collision.

### Active
- Fix or clarify the browser test’s final return-to-panel win check; it ended with `VERBINDUNG VERLOREN.` instead of the expected win.
- Inspect the latest JPEG screenshot and check browser errors after resolving the test.
- Confirm unused `game.liftDelay` removal if applicable.

### Blocked
- The final win assertion fails; suspected simulated timer updates also trigger a loss condition before the panel interaction.

## Next Move
1. Diagnose why the simulated sequence ends in `VERBINDUNG VERLOREN.` before validating the return-to-panel interaction.
2. Rerun browser verification, confirm the win interaction and no browser errors, then inspect the latest JPEG at `/tmp/opencode/facility-verification.jpg`.
3. Recheck `node --check src/game.js`, `git diff --check`, and `git status --short`.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Modified audio helpers, elevator interactions, gameplay loop, and sound UI handlers.
- `index.html`: Sound toggle and volume control.
- `/tmp/opencode/verify-facility.mjs`: Temporary Playwright verification script for sound and elevator behavior.
- `/tmp/opencode/facility-verification.jpg`: Captured verification screenshot; inspection still pending.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; earlier `git status --short` showed only `M src/game.js`.
- Remote preview URL `https://live-42481859356-1.omgithub.com` returned HTTP 404; local HTTP server on port 8765 was used for browser testing.
- Playwright requires `DISPLAY=:0` in this environment.
